page_notes.content: Preserve the page's existing structure and Mermaid-diagram style while making the architectural fit explicit. Cover these implementation details from hardcover/lib/bookshelf_sources.lua and main.lua: (1) Registration lifecycle — Sources.register(app) is called during plugin init in main.lua around lines 313-316 and retried with UIManager:nextTick if Bookshelf is not loaded yet; Sources.register returns false cleanly when app.ui.bookshelf is absent or bookshelf.SOURCE_API < 1 (bookshelf_sources.lua around lines 652-659), making the integration optional. (2) Refresh pipeline — startLoad (around lines 390-415) deduplicates in-flight loads by key, applies a 30-second retry_after backoff after failures, and runs loaders through UIManager:nextTick plus Background.run so network work does not block the UI tick. (3) Change notification — changed()/changedShelf() (around lines 376-388) call bookshelf:sourceChanged(id) so Bookshelf re-renders; sign-out in main.lua (around lines 303-310) clears the account-scoped review_store, shelf_cache, and book_store (leaving shelf_store and list_store intact), signs out, and calls BookshelfSources.changed(self). (4) Remote book routing — remoteSpec (around lines 634-650) declares remote_prefix "hardcover://", owns() matching ^hardcover://book/, and open/info handlers that route through bookDetail (around lines 627-632) to app.dialog_manager:showBookDetail(book_id). (5) Architectural position — present bookshelf_sources.lua as a presentation-layer bridge: it reads cached/shared state from shelf_store, shelf_cache, and list_store, converts records for Bookshelf, and pushes sourceChanged notifications into Bookshelf, while network requests and persistence remain in the shared Api/ShelfLoader/store infrastructure. Mention that the related but separate bookshelf_modules/ micro-module pack is covered on page 5.2, not here. Keep coverage of registration, lazy fetching, fingerprints, covers, and offline behavior, and cite source files and lines in the wiki's usual style.
